rules.statement: When a decision record is marked superseded, keep any earlier partial-supersession pointers in its status line and its decisions-index row alongside the new superseding record (e.g. "Superseded by ADR-B (its protection was already superseded by ADR-A)").
rules.why: Without the earlier pointer, someone who reads the superseded record first gets an incomplete history of it.
rules.check: In a diff that changes an ADR's status to Superseded, compare against the old status: if it mentioned another record that had already overturned part of it, confirm that pointer survives in the new status and in the index row.

rules.statement: When references to a superseded decision record are replaced, point each one at every record that now owns the decision it cited, not just one of them.
rules.why: Dropping one of the replacements means the document no longer links to part of the decision, such as the release-line record.
rules.check: In a diff that replaces citations of a superseded ADR in README or config comments, confirm each citation names every successor record relevant to what that text is about.

rules.statement: Keep edited comment lines within the wrap width the rest of that comment block uses (about 120 columns), rewrapping so text moves to the next line.
rules.why: A line past the block's width means the next reflow of that comment has to touch it again.
rules.check: Look for edited comment lines in config or source files that are noticeably longer than the neighbouring lines of the same comment block.
